chain.link: Orf6-NUP98 (viral bait -> human prey; KEPT edge)
chain.claim: SARS-CoV-2 Orf6 binds the nucleoporin Nup98. Orf6's C-terminal acidic tail docks onto the Nup98-Rae1 complex; Miorin et al. show Orf6 hijacks Nup98 to block STAT1/STAT2 nuclear import and antagonize interferon signaling. Present as a high-confidence AP-MS interaction in the Gordon interactome.

chain.link: Orf6-RAE1 (viral bait -> human prey; HELD-OUT edge to recover)
chain.claim: SARS-CoV-2 Orf6 also directly engages Rae1. Addetia et al. (mBio) show Orf6 interacts with Rae1 (and Nup98) to disrupt bidirectional nucleocytoplasmic transport; Li et al. (Mol Biol Cell) show Orf6 is positioned in the nuclear pore complex by Rae1; Kehrer/Gao structural work resolves the Orf6 C-terminus bound at the Rae1-Nup98 interface.

chain.link: NUP98-RAE1 (human-human bridge; STRING edge that enables L3 recovery)
chain.claim: Nup98 and Rae1 form a documented, conserved mRNA-export complex at the nuclear pore. Rae1 (mrnp41) is a shuttling mRNA export factor that binds a GLEBS-like motif of Nup98 (Pritchard 1999); Ren et al. solved the crystal structure of the Nup98-Rae1 complex (2010); the same Rae1-Nup98 nucleic-acid-binding surface is targeted by viral antagonists such as VSV matrix protein (Quan 2014), the mechanistic precedent Orf6 mimics.

mechanism_summary: Rae1 and Nup98 form a conserved heterodimeric mRNA-export platform at the cytoplasmic face of the nuclear pore complex (Pritchard 1999 PMID 10209021; Ren 2010 PMID 20498086). SARS-CoV-2 Orf6 docks its short acidic C-terminal tail (Met58/di-acidic motif) directly onto this Rae1-Nup98 complex, occupying the same interface used by cellular transport factors and by the VSV matrix protein (Quan 2014 PMID 24927547). By tethering to Rae1-Nup98 at the pore, Orf6 blocks bidirectional nucleocytoplasmic transport (Addetia 2021 PMID 33849972; Li 2024 PMID 38507240), preventing import of activated STAT1/STAT2 and thereby antagonizing type I/III interferon signaling (Miorin 2020 PMID 33097660). Because Orf6 binds BOTH partners of the same human complex, holding out Orf6-RAE1 while keeping Orf6-NUP98 and adding the human NUP98-RAE1 bridge yields the length-3 path Orf6 -> NUP98 -> RAE1, so degree-normalized L3 recovers the held-out Orf6-RAE1 edge. The bridge is mechanistically real (a physical complex), not a coincidental network shortcut.

backup_example.note: Alternative worked example in a mitochondrial/innate-immunity neighborhood.

chain.claim: SARS-CoV-2 Orf9b binds the mitochondrial import receptor TOM70 (TOMM70). Reported in the Gordon AP-MS map and resolved structurally (cryo-EM Orf9b-Tom70) in Gordon 2020 Science; Jiang 2020 shows Orf9b suppresses type I interferon by targeting TOM70; Orf9b binding blocks the TOM70-HSP90 interaction needed for MAVS/TBK1-IRF3 signaling.

backup_example.candidate_bridge: TOMM70-HSP90AA1 (human chaperone-receptor interaction) would serve as the L3 bridge if Orf9b-TOMM70 were held out and an Orf9b->HSP90->TOMM70 path exists in the enriched graph.
backup_example.mechanism_summary: Orf9b occupies the substrate-binding pocket of TOM70, displacing HSP90 and blunting TOM70-dependent activation of the MAVS antiviral signaling axis, suppressing type I IFN (Jiang 2020 PMID 32728199; Ayinde 2022 PMID 35643212).

verification_method: Every PMID resolved via NCBI E-utilities esummary (db=pubmed, JSON); each record's title and DOI were read from the same authoritative PubMed record, co-verifying PMID<->DOI<->title. PMC8092196 resolved to PMID 33849972 / DOI 10.1128/mBio.00065-21 via NCBI ID Converter.
